vos.title: Only the Strongs Survive
vos.subTitle:
Five years as a Binance Angel… and this one feels special. 🏆
When I joined the Binance Angels program back in 2020, I honestly had no idea where this journey would take mew
Since then there have been countless hours helping users, answering questions, supporting communities, creating content, attending events, testing things, reporting problems, giving feedback, solving the occasional disaster 😅… and, more importantly, meeting people from all over the world who somehow became part of the same crazy Binance family.
It hasn’t always been an easy road.
Five years is a long time in crypto.
Markets change. Teams change. Communities change. Platforms change. Sometimes you are extremely active, sometimes life takes over, sometimes you wonder whether all those hours behind the scenes are really noticed.
But I kept doing it because I genuinely enjoy being useful.
Over the years I’ve been nominated several times in the Binance Angels Awards, particularly around content, community and contribution to the ecosystem.
This year was probably my most diverse one yet.
I was nominated for:
🤖 AI Master

📣 Social Advocate

🧩 Problem Solver

💡 Feedback Master
Four very different categories, which actually made me smile because they describe pretty well what my last few years as an Angel have looked like.
I create things.
I break things.
I question things.
And then I normally try to figure out how to fix them. 😂
And this year I finally came home with the:

🏆 Problem Solver Award
Out of all the categories, this one probably represents me better than any other.
I have never been the guy who just says, “this doesn’t work.”
My brain immediately goes:

Why doesn’t it work?

Where is the problem?

Can we reproduce it?

Can we improve it?

Is there another way to do it?
Sometimes that probably makes me a pain in the ass. 😅
But apparently, after five years, someone decided that was worth an award.
So this one genuinely means a lot.
Not because of the trophy itself, but because it represents five years of showing up, learning, helping, experimenting and trying to leave things a little better than I found them.
Huge congratulations as well to all the other Binance Angels who were nominated and to everyone who won this year. There are people in this program doing incredible work quietly every single day.
And thank you to the Binance team and everyone behind the Angels program who has been part of this journey.

Five years later…
Still here.

Still curious.

Still causing problems.

Still solving them. 😏

🏆 Problem Solver 2026
Not a bad way to celebrate five years as a Binance Angel. 🔶

vos.title: Zcash (ZEC) Short Squeeze Liquidates Trader 0x3c83's $1M Bet
vos.subTitle:
• Trader 0x3c83 saw a 767.2 ZEC short worth $1 million fully liquidated.
• Zcash rallied from $1,101 to an intraday high of $1,396, a 17% surge.
• Paradigm co-founder Matt Huang disclosed ZEC holdings, calling Zcash a privacy complement to Bitcoin.
$1M Short Wiped Out in ZEC Squeeze
Privacy-focused Zcash (ZEC) delivered one of the sharpest short squeezes of the week, and on-chain data tracked by Lookonchain shows exactly how expensive betting against it became. A trader known on-chain as 0x3c83 closed out an existing long position and flipped bearish, opening a short of 767.2 ZEC — sized at roughly $1 million at entry — only to see the entire position forcibly liquidated within hours as the coin's momentum turned vertical.
Market data shows ZEC ripping from $1,101 to $1,383 in a near-parabolic session before printing an intraday high of $1,396, a 17% advance that gave the bearish bet no room to breathe. Liquidations in the leverage-driven derivatives market occur when price moves sharply against a position and its collateral no longer covers margin requirements, forcing the exchange to close the trade and frequently wiping out the full stake. In this case, the squeeze became self-reinforcing: forced buy-backs from liquidated shorts absorbed bearish order flow and added fuel to the rally, producing the kind of violent volatility that makes oversized leveraged positions effectively unmanageable. The move capped a run that had already pushed the Zcash topic hub into focus earlier this week, when the coin broke above $1,290, its highest level since November 2016. It also stands in sharp contrast to the prior deleveraging episode, when longs absorbed a $23.75M liquidation wave during a 16% pullback — a reminder that both sides of this market have been running hot.
Paradigm's Matt Huang Backs Zcash
While traders counted liquidations, institutional validation arrived from a different direction. Paradigm co-founder Matt Huang publicly disclosed that the venture firm is a ZEC holder on top of its investment in the Zcash Open Development Lab (ZODL), framing the asset as a “privacy complement to Bitcoin.” Huang argued that most blockchain ecosystems chronically underfund long-term public-goods development, and that sustaining a stable developer fund becomes more urgent as AI-driven cyberattacks and quantum computing capabilities advance — though he conceded the fund's allocation mechanics remain open to improvement.
His remarks on governance were equally pointed: if Zcash sees broader adoption as a monetary asset, token-holder voting alone could inject uncertainty into its long-term credibility, so he favors combining coin-vote mechanisms with other governance structures. The comments landed just as holders wrapped up the NU7 upgrade vote, backing 25-second target block times by an overwhelming margin while preserving the existing halving and issuance schedule. Paradigm's involvement is not new — in March, ZODL announced a seed round exceeding $25 million with Paradigm, a16z crypto, Coinbase Ventures and Winklevoss Capital participating, alongside earlier backing that includes the Grayscale ZCSH fund crossing $500M in assets. The price backdrop explains the attention: ZEC gained roughly 160% over the past month versus Bitcoin's 18.2%, and Glassnode data shows the privacy-coin sector has risen about 213% from Bitcoin's October 2025 peak — roughly 85% even excluding ZEC, per altcoin sector trackers.
$1,559 Resistance Is the Next Test
COINOTAG's proprietary 42-indicator composite S/R scoring engine rates the $1,558.88 resistance at 85/100, driven by the confluence of R1, ATR Upper and Donchian Upper — and spot at $1,509.44, up 10.65% over 24 hours, is pressing directly beneath it. A daily candlestick close above $1,558.88 opens the path toward $1,869.52; losing the $1,263.80 support (63/100, Flip R→S, Ichimoku Tenkan) invalidates the bullish read. RSI at 73.45 signals overbought conditions despite a bullish MACD, while funding at -0.0089% on $1.286B in open interest shows shorts still paying to hold — squeeze fuel that could carry price higher, with Fear & Greed at 56 (Greed).

vos.title: 🚨 Bitcoin Survived the Fed Hike. What Comes Next?
vos.subTitle:
The Fed just delivered its first rate hike since 2023.
25 bps higher. Policy rate now at 3.75%–4.00%.
Yet $BTC didn't collapse.
That tells us something important:
The market was already prepared for this move.
The bigger risk may not be the hike itself.
It may be what happens next.
📌 Inflation stays sticky
📌 The Fed sees at least one more hike in 2026
📌 Treasury yields remain elevated
📌 The dollar and liquidity conditions can tighten
📌 A fresh energy or geopolitical shock could add more inflation pressure
Reuters reported that 16 of 18 Fed policymakers expect at least one more hike this year, while the Fed's latest projections put 2026 PCE inflation at 3.7%.
So the key question for $BTC isn't simply:
"Will the Fed hike again?"
It's:
Will the next move be more hawkish than the market expects?
That's where things could get interesting.
If inflation cools and yields stabilize, Bitcoin may continue absorbing restrictive policy.
But if inflation reaccelerates, yields surge and markets suddenly price a longer period of tight policy, risk assets could face a much tougher environment.
And this is the signal I'm watching most:
How does $BTC react to bad macro news?
If bad news keeps getting absorbed without a major breakdown, that's information.
If every negative macro headline starts producing deeper selloffs, that's information too.
The reaction matters more than the headline.
No need to chase. Watch liquidity, yields, the dollar and $BTC structure.

vos.subTitle:
Stocks and bonds climbed Thursday as a second straight drop in oil prices eased worries about how much further the Federal Reserve will need to go to keep inflation in check. The ral‍ly came a day after the c‌entral bank rais‌ed inter​e​s‌t ra⁠tes⁠ for t‍he first time since‍ 2023,‌ a decis‍ion t‍h‍at b‍riefly rattled market​s⁠ b‌e‌fore Wednesday's close. Tech stocks le‌d the rebound, givi‌ng​ investors some relief after a stretch battered by in⁠fla⁠tion anxiety, the rate decision itself,‌ and‌ the still grindin⁠g war in the Mi⁠ddle East‌. 
Bonds got a lift too. The 10-year Treasury yield dropped more than seven basis points to 4.93%, slipping back below the 5% mark it had crossed a day earlier in the hours following the Fed's announcement.

Oil fell for a second consecutive session on signs that the supply tightness gripping the market since the war began may be starting to loosen, as parts of the disruption in the Middle East show early signs of easing. Word that Saudi Arabia is racing to restore roughly half the capacity of its East-West pipeline within days, after drone strikes forced its shutdown last week, took some of the edge off fears of vanishing crude cargoes tied to the Iran conflict. West Texas Intermediate settled 0.51% lower, at $101.91 a barrel. Brent slid 0.95%, to $104.82.

President Trump struck an optimistic note on where the war stands. Speaking to reporters in North Carolina Wednesday evening, he said, "Hopefully we are toward the end of the war," adding that Iran wants a deal and that he had spoken with Tehran directly. He did not say what those conversations involved.
The rally sh​o‌wed up‌ acros⁠s‍ every major ind‍ex. The  broad S&P 5⁠00 index climbe‍d 1.1%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq​ Composite jumped 1.7%‌. Ev‌en the small-cap Russell 2⁠000 joi⁠ned in, addi‍ng 0.‍6% to‍ close at 2,874.‌46, while the 30-stock Dow ta‍cked on 0.​6%​ o⁠f its own.

Technology did the heavy lifting. Micron shares rose more than 5% after Intel's CEO said memory chip demand isn't slowing and that prices would keep climbing, a remark that lifted Nvidia, Broadcom and SK Hynix alongside it. Investors read that as confirmation that pricing power in memory holds even as AI capex costs climb. Nvidia and Amazon, two of the so-called Magnificent Seven, each rose more than 2%. Microsoft added 1.5%. Elsewhere in the AI trade, Qualcomm gained 2%, and Intel jumped 7%.

Chipmaker Marvell Technology added 4.8%.  Corning, the glassmaker whose fiber optics have quietly become an AI infrastructure staple, climbed 2.5% as well. Storage names Seagate Technology and Western Digital each gained 2.6% and 1.7%, respectively.

General Motors spent the day making a different kind of case, one built on pistons instead of software. The automaker unveiled a new 6.6-liter, sixth-generation small-block V-8 for the 2027 Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra, aimed squarely at Ford and Ram at a moment when EV demand has cooled. GM shares rose 2.76%, closing at $86.62.

Workday climbed 6% after CNBC's David Faber reported that financing for a possible deal to take the human resources software company private is still moving forward, citing people familiar with the effort.

Lucid Group added almost 6% after its chief executive told Bloomberg that the company's restructuring work with outside advisers has wrapped up, according to FactSet.

SiTime jumped nearly 10% after Morgan Stanley initiated coverage with an overweight rating and a $730 price target, implying 33% upside from Wednesday's close. The Silicon Valley company makes MEMS-based silicon timing chips, the unglamorous parts that keep data centers running on schedule.

Copper Keeps Flirting With Records
Copper doesn't get the headlines Nvidia does. Maybe it should. The met‍al touched​ an‍ intraday h​igh of $6.6150 a p​ound Thursda⁠y‍, its‌ strongest level since Sept​em‌ber 10, when i⁠t reach‍ed $6.8915. That‌'s sti‌ll sh⁠y o​f the all time intraday pe⁠ak‌ of $6.894, set just a day e⁠arlier, on Septem​ber 9. Cop‍per is up roug‍hly 1⁠% for the wee⁠k, putting it on pace for it‌s third positive week in the last four. Copper miners rose on the news, its first up day in six. Shares of Freeport-McMoRan and Southern Copper closed 2.3% and 3.2%, respectively. BHP Group rose nearly 3% while Hudbay Minerals climbed by 4.7%

The story looked similar in London. LME copper climbed to $14,433 a metric ton, the highest level since September 10, when it touched $14,875, itself the exchange's intraday record. 
The day's biggest individual mover was Generac. Shares climbed 18% after the generator maker struck a long-term supply deal with Amazon to provide backup power for its data centers, with initial deliveries expected to total $2.4 billion between 2027 and 2028. As part of the arrangement, Generac also granted Amazon the right to buy up to $340 million worth of its stock. Amazon's own shares moved 1.3% higher on the news.

Fluence Energy went the other direction, tumbling 15% after the battery storage maker slashed⁠ its full-year guidance. T⁠he comp​a⁠ny now expects $2.4 billion in​ r​evenue for fiscal 20‌26, down from‍ prior guidance‌ of $2‍.9 bil‍lion to $3.1 billi⁠on​, an​d an EB‌ITD​A loss of roughly $‍20‍0 milli⁠on⁠, a sharp reversal fro‌m a previ‌o⁠us‌ range spanning a $30 million l‍oss to​ a $10 million g‌ain.

Sector Analysis:
Wall Street shook off its Fed hangover on Thursday. Information Technology led the board, up 2.20%, as chipmakers reversed Wednesday's rate-hike rout on a single data point. Its stocks rose after Intel's CEO said memory chip demand isn't slowing and that prices would keep climbing, a remark that lifted Nvidia, Broadcom and SK Hynix alongside it. Investors read that as confirmation that pricing power in memory holds even as AI capex costs climb. 
Consumer Discretionary added 1.43%, powered less by shopping data than by the bond market: homebuilders gained ground after housing data showed single-family housing starts and pending home sales increased, giving the group room to breathe after weeks of pressure from mortgage rates near 7%. 
Utilities rose 0.86%, extending a rally that owes more to growth than to defense — the sector has spent 2026 trading on data-center electricity demand rather than its old bond-proxy script, and Thursday's retreat in yields removed one of its few remaining headwinds. None of this looks accidental. It extends themes that have defined the year: an AI buildout hungry for chips and power, and a housing market waiting for any excuse to rally.
Worst-Performing Sectors
Consumer Staples and Financials barely moved, down 0.01% and 0.10% — sectors left behind rather than sold off. Staples' flatness reflected where money went, not where it fled: with risk appetite back, capital rotated into chips and housing and left grocery, beverage and household-product names to drift without a catalyst of their own. Financials fared little better, stabilizing rather than recovering after Wednesday's 2.3% selloff that followed the Fed's first rate hike in three years. 
Sentiment wasn't helped by Goldman Sachs flagging a softer fixed-income, currencies and commodities quarter even as its equities business held up. Both moves read as sector-wide rather than stock-specific — no single name dragged either group down, and the weakness looks more like fatigue than a fresh negative catalyst.
Whether Thursday's calm holds depends on plenty that no earnings call can settle. The Fed has already signaled another hike is coming before year's end, and Trump's own optimism about the war comes with a hedge built into the first word: hopefully.

vos.title: Charles Schwab Favors Commodities Over Bonds on $13.4 Trillion Book, Bitcoin (BTC) in Focus
vos.subTitle:
• Charles Schwab holds a neutral equity stance, favoring commodities over bonds, strategist Liz Ann Sonders says.
• Schwab oversees $13.4 trillion in client assets with no universal allocation recommended.
• Gold-backed ETFs took in $18 billion in August, the second-biggest monthly inflow on record.
Liz Ann Sonders: No Cookie-Cutter Allocation
Charles Schwab, the brokerage overseeing $13.4 trillion in client assets, is telling investors there is no single portfolio formula for this market cycle. Chief investment strategist Liz Ann Sonders laid out the firm's house view in a recent interview: neutral on equities, less favorable on fixed income, and comparatively more constructive on commodities. Allocation, she argued, should hinge on each investor's time horizon, risk tolerance, income needs and overall goals, not on a preset template. “It drives me a little crazy,” she said, “when people give a cookie-cutter answer,” adding that no one asset allocation “makes sense right now.” Her pushback targets the classic 60/40 portfolio, the benchmark mix of 60% stocks and 40% bonds that has anchored retirement planning for decades and that other strategists now want to rebuild around hard assets. The mix assumes bonds reliably offset equity drawdowns, an assumption that has been tested repeatedly in recent cycles. Sonders pointed to Schwab's sheer scale as evidence that no single answer fits every client; a book that size, she suggested, is exactly why personalized allocation beats any universal split. She framed the neutral equity stance as positioning rather than a call to sell, stressing that neutrality is “not a bearish position” and simply reflects the firm's long-term strategic allocation. The neutrality spans the entire equity sleeve rather than any single corner of the market: it applies as much to semiconductor names such as Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and Applied Materials (AMAT) as to healthcare shares like Eli Lilly (LLY). Other strategists have floated carving a bigger slice for commodities, including a 60/20/20 split that would put a fifth of a portfolio into real assets. Sonders declined to endorse any fixed ratio, saying the right percentages depend on goals, horizon and income needs, with age and investor profile mattering just as much.
Gold ETFs Pulled In $18 Billion in August
The commodities tilt lands against a striking hard-asset backdrop. World Gold Council data, the industry record of global gold demand, shows gold-backed exchange-traded funds absorbed $18 billion in August alone, the second-biggest monthly inflow on record, and lifted total fund holdings to an all-time high. Only one month in history has seen a larger net inflow, and cumulative holdings now stand above every prior peak, a combination of pace and level that allocators rarely witness in a single asset class at once. Gold ETFs hold physical bullion on behalf of shareholders, so portfolio demand translates directly into bullion buying, which is why the record matters beyond fund flows. Strategists read the surge as a hedge against fiscal deficits and currency debasement, positioning gold as the default store of value outside traditional financial plumbing. The flows mark a visible institutional step away from the traditional stock-bond duopoly and toward tangible assets at a moment when the 60/40 benchmark is under its widest scrutiny in years. Schwab's stance echoes that broader rotation: the firm is simply less favorable on fixed income and more favorable on commodities, a pairing Sonders presented as a deliberate tilt rather than a wholesale exit from either asset class. The debate over whether stock-bond diversification still works is far from settled, and the 60/20/20 proposals circulating among strategists show how far the conversation has drifted from the old consensus. Whether the tilt proves prescient will depend on how the current cycle for gold and other real assets plays out in the months ahead. For diversified investors, the shift cuts across the whole traditional book, from US semiconductors to Chinese e-commerce names such as Alibaba (BABA), because a sustained real-asset rotation reprices the opportunity cost of holding equities at all.
A Hard-Asset Rotation Bitcoin (BTC) Can Ride
The throughline in both developments is a quiet rotation out of the stock-bond duopoly and into real assets, and Bitcoin (BTC) sits on the same fault line. Gold's record $18 billion August inflow, documented in the World Gold Council's demand data, is the hardest datapoint: institutional money is moving before strategists finish debating the 60/40 mix. Our reading of the flow picture is that BTC, changing hands near $77,547 at press time, has historically behaved as a higher-beta expression of the same debasement trade now filling gold funds. If Schwab's commodities preference marks a durable allocation shift across $13.4 trillion in advised assets, digital hard assets are positioned to share the bid.

vos.title: Bitcoin Survived the Fed Hike So What Could Actually Break the Market Now❓❓
vos.subTitle:
Bitcoin just passed one of September's biggest tests.....

The Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 basis points on September 16, taking the target range to 3.75%–4.00%. It was the first Fed hike since 2023.

Normally, that is exactly the kind of event capable of creating serious pressure across risk markets.

But Bitcoin didn't collapse.

BTC remained around the upper-$70,000 area on September 17, showing that much of the expected Fed move had already been absorbed by the market.

So if a Fed hike couldn't immediately break Bitcoin, the more interesting question becomes:

What actually could?

Another Rate Hike Could Be More Important Than This One

The September hike wasn't necessarily the end of the story.

The Fed's new projections showed a median federal-funds rate of 4.1% at the end of 2026, while 16 of 18 policymakers expected at least one more quarter-point increase this year.

That matters because markets had plenty of time to prepare for September.

The next hike could become more disruptive if investors aren't expecting it.

Crypto doesn't simply react to whether rates rise or fall. It reacts to the difference between what investors expected and what actually happens.

If markets suddenly begin pricing a longer period of tight monetary policy, Bitcoin could face a much tougher environment.

Inflation Is Still the Real Problem

The Fed didn't raise rates for no reason.

Its September projections put 2026 PCE inflation at 3.7% and core PCE inflation at 3.4%, both still well above the Fed's 2% objective.

That means inflation remains one of the biggest macro risks for crypto.

Imagine another unexpectedly hot inflation report.

Traders could quickly start pricing additional Fed tightening. Treasury yields could rise. The dollar could strengthen. Risk appetite could weaken.

One inflation report wouldn't automatically crash Bitcoin, but a series of hotter-than-expected readings could change the entire liquidity narrative.

That may be a bigger threat than the September hike itself.

Treasury Yields Are Getting Hard to Ignore

Crypto traders spend hours watching Bitcoin support and resistance.

Right now, they should probably keep one eye on the bond market too.

The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.00% on September 15, while the 30-year yield stood at 5.36%, according to Federal Reserve data.

Higher yields create competition for capital.

When relatively safer assets offer attractive returns, investors have less reason to move aggressively into volatile assets.

Bitcoin managed to rally from its late-August lows even while yields remained elevated, but that doesn't mean it is immune to them. Reuters noted before the Fed meeting that renewed inflation concerns and rising bond yields remained important risks to BTC's recovery.

If yields push significantly higher again, the pressure could eventually become harder for crypto to ignore.

Leverage Could Turn a Normal Drop Into Something Bigger

Sometimes Bitcoin doesn't need terrible news to fall hard.

It simply needs too many traders positioned in the same direction.

The latest Fed move demonstrated how quickly leveraged positions can disappear. Roughly $345 million in crypto derivatives positions were liquidated over a 24-hour period surrounding the decision, according to market data reported September 17.

This is why leverage matters.

If traders become extremely confident after Bitcoin survives the Fed decision, more leveraged long positions can build.

Then even a normal correction can begin triggering liquidations.

Those forced sales push prices lower, which can trigger another group of liquidations.

A small move can suddenly become a much larger one.

The dangerous moment isn't always when everyone is scared.

Sometimes it comes when everyone becomes too comfortable.

Institutional Demand Could Also Change

One reason Bitcoin has been able to absorb difficult macro conditions is continued institutional interest.

Ahead of the Fed meeting, Reuters reported renewed inflows into U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs as BTC recovered from roughly $60,000 in late August to above $70,000.

That demand matters.

If institutional flows remain healthy, sellers have another source of buyers waiting on the other side.

But flows can reverse.

Persistent ETF outflows combined with weaker spot demand would change the picture considerably.

A falling market with strong underlying demand can recover.

A falling market while major sources of demand are disappearing is a different situation entirely.

That's why traders should watch not only Bitcoin's price but also who is buying behind that price.

A Wider Liquidity Shock Would Be the Bigger Test

The biggest threat may not come from crypto at all.

It could come from traditional financial markets.

Bitcoin still exists inside a global financial system where stocks, bonds, currencies and commodities compete for capital.

A sudden economic shock, geopolitical escalation or broader rush toward cash could force investors to reduce risk across multiple markets simultaneously.

During those moments, correlations can change quickly.

Assets that normally behave differently can suddenly fall together because investors aren't asking which asset has the strongest narrative.

They're looking for liquidity.

Bitcoin surviving a predictable 25-basis-point Fed hike therefore doesn't prove that it would survive a genuine global liquidity shock with the same strength.

Those are two very different events.

The Most Important Signal Is Bitcoin's Reaction

There is another way to look at all of this.

Bad news alone doesn't determine price.

The market's reaction to bad news does.

Bitcoin fell to around $60,000 in late August before recovering above $70,000 ahead of the Fed meeting. Despite inflation concerns, high Treasury yields and expectations of tighter monetary policy, buyers returned.

That resilience deserves attention.

But it shouldn't create overconfidence.

If another negative catalyst arrives and Bitcoin suddenly stops absorbing the selling, that change in behavior could matter more than the headline itself.

So What Could Actually Break Bitcoin's Strength?

Probably not one headline by itself.

The more serious scenario would be several pressures arriving together.

Persistent inflation.

More aggressive Fed tightening.

Rising Treasury yields.

Weakening institutional demand.

Heavy leverage.

And a break in Bitcoin's underlying market structure.

Any one of those could create volatility.

Several happening together could create something much larger.

For now, Bitcoin has survived the Fed's first rate hike since 2023.

That is notable.

But the real test isn't whether Bitcoin can survive news the market already expected.

The real test comes when something arrives that the market isn't prepared for.

vos.title: $XRP Is Holding $1.29 — But The Real Test Is $1.34
vos.subTitle:
The interesting part of XRP right now isn't simply the recovery toward $1.30.

It's what happened after the sharp September selloff.

XRP dropped from around $1.42 toward $1.28 on September 15. Since then, price has stabilized around $1.29–$1.31 instead of immediately breaking lower.

That makes $1.29 the level I'm watching first.

The bigger story is spot resilience vs. derivatives deleveraging.

XRP futures open interest has fallen sharply, from roughly $1.13B to around $871M. That's a significant reduction in leverage.

But here's the important distinction:

Falling OI doesn't automatically mean traders became bearish.

It can also mean the market simply flushed excessive leverage.

Funding has moved much closer to neutral, while positioning is no longer as crowded as it was during the previous move.

For me, that's actually more interesting than a simple bullish or bearish signal.

THE CHART STRUCTURE

$1.29–$1.30 is the immediate battleground.

If buyers can keep defending this zone, the next important reclaim is around $1.34.

Above $1.34, XRP would have a better chance of testing $1.40, which is much stronger resistance from the recent breakdown.

But if $1.29 fails and price cannot reclaim it, the $1.25–$1.26 area becomes important again.

That's where the recent selloff found stronger buying interest.

THE FUNDAMENTAL SIDE

XRPL development hasn't stopped during the price weakness.

The latest XRPL 3.4.0 release adds improvements around the Lending Protocol, including expanded vault functionality and accounting changes.

That's constructive for the network's infrastructure.

But I wouldn't automatically translate network development into XRP price appreciation.

That's the distinction I'm watching:

XRPL adoption can grow without every unit of that growth immediately creating XRP demand.

There is also still a supply consideration. Ripple continues to manage XRP through its escrow system, so future releases remain part of the longer-term supply equation.

BULLISH SCENARIO

XRP holds $1.29–$1.30.

Then price reclaims $1.34 with stronger spot volume.

That would make $1.40 the next major test.

I would want the breakout to come with participation rather than simply a thin liquidity move.

BEARISH SCENARIO

XRP loses $1.29 and fails to reclaim it.

Then $1.25–$1.26 becomes the next important zone.

A clean break below that area would weaken the current recovery structure considerably.

WHAT I LIKE

Derivatives leverage has been flushed.

Price is still holding above the recent selloff low.

XRPL development continues.

Institutional access to XRP has expanded.

WHAT I DON'T LIKE

$1.34–$1.40 remains heavy resistance.

The recovery has not yet produced a convincing higher-high structure.

Lower OI means leverage has reset, but it also means aggressive new positioning hasn't fully returned.

Personally, I wouldn't chase XRP around $1.30.

I want to see what happens at the edges.

$1.34 reclaimed with volume = recovery becomes more credible.

$1.29 lost = downside structure comes back into focus.

Right now, XRP is rebuilding after a leverage flush.

The market still needs to prove that this is more than just a bounce.

Can XRP turn $1.30 from a stabilization zone into a real launchpad

vos.title: Shiba Inu (SHIB) Records Net Spot Outflows Across All 7 Timeframes, $206K Exits in 24 Hours
vos.subTitle:
• Shiba Inu (SHIB) logged net spot outflows across all seven timeframes from 1 hour to 3 months
• SHIB fell more than 10% from the September 13 high of $0.0000142 to $0.0000127
• SHIB open interest dropped 6.44% to $119.4 million
SHIB Grinds Below Key Resistance
Shiba Inu (SHIB) is trading in one of the tightest ranges across the altcoin market, with short-term momentum failing to produce a decisive break in either direction. The memecoin has spent the session pressed against a dense cluster of moving averages, and repeated attempts to clear the $0.0000051 to $0.0000052 band — the short-term chart's most closely watched resistance zone — have come up short since late August. Price tested that shelf several times without establishing acceptance above it, keeping the technical picture fragile. The September rejection near $0.00000555 left a sequence of lower highs behind, and until the $0.0000051–$0.0000052 band gives way, structure argues the market has not yet reclaimed control of its trend. One feature of the setup stands out: multiple moving averages converge inside the $0.0000049 to $0.0000051 corridor, meaning both short- and medium-term trend measures now sit almost on top of spot price. Trading volume has contracted visibly, and the FOMO-suppressed relative strength index hovering near the 50 midpoint signals that neither buyers nor sellers have secured directional confirmation. On the downside, holding the $0.0000049–$0.0000050 shelf would preserve the current compression, a floor we tracked in recent coverage of the $0.0000050 support range. A decisive loss of that zone would open $0.0000047–$0.0000046 first, with $0.0000044 the next downside objective. The upside scenario requires more: SHIB must push through $0.0000052 and defend that break before a retest of $0.0000055 becomes realistic. The congestion mirrors a broader split among major assets — Ethereum consolidating sideways after its August advance, Dogecoin repeatedly turned back from $0.090–$0.092, while only a handful of tokens such as Zcash have sustained fresh momentum.
Spot Outflows Hit Every Timeframe
Flow data supplies the bearish counterpoint to that technical stalemate. Aggregated spot-flow figures from CoinGlass show Shiba Inu recording net outflows across every one of seven analytical windows — the 1-hour, 4-hour, 12-hour, 24-hour, 1-week, 1-month and 3-month charts — meaning money has been leaving regardless of holding horizon. In the most recent 24-hour stretch alone, roughly $206,000 in SHIB flowed out of spot venues, cementing sell-side dominance across both short-term trading books and longer-term holdings. Price action has followed the money. After tagging a local high of $0.0000142 on September 13, SHIB slid day after day to the $0.0000127 line, a drawdown of more than 10% from the peak, with each bounce met by willing sellers and short-term support failing to hold. The futures side of the market has cooled in step: open interest fell 6.44% from the prior day to roughly $119.4 million, while derivatives volume managed only around $240 million — evidence that leveraged positions were closed or trimmed rather than rolled, draining the liquidity a genuine rebound would need. That deleveraging matters given SHIB's holder profile; our earlier reporting showed 808 whale wallets controlling 94.68% of circulating supply, so exit pressure from even a modest slice of large holders can overwhelm retail demand. The recovery checklist this data implies is specific: spot exchanges must flip back to net inflows and open interest must rebuild before any bounce can be trusted. Our read of on-chain activity points the same way — rising transfers without bullish confirmation — and as long as outflows persist across all seven windows, further price adjustment cannot be ruled out. This flow snapshot, stamped later in the session than the chart work above, is the freshest reading on where SHIB stands.
Composite Scores Frame the Next Move
For positioning, COINOTAG's proprietary 42-indicator composite S/R scoring engine frames the battleground precisely: the strongest resistance — a Fibonacci 0.382 retracement — rates 57/100 on our composite scoring engine, with the Fibonacci 0.236 level adding a 46/100 layer just below. Support is nearly as firm: the Fibonacci 0.500 retracement scores 51/100, while a swing-low and Ichimoku Tenkan/Kijun confluence contribute a 48/100 cluster. Momentum is undecided — RSI at 54.48, MACD neutral, trend classified sideways — while perp funding at +0.0056% signals a mild long bias and our Fear and Greed Index reads 56/100, in Greed. The bullish case needs a break above the 57/100 Fibonacci 0.382 wall; losing the 48-score Ichimoku cluster would invalidate it.

vos.title: Taking a Look at Bubblemaps V2
vos.subTitle:
I’ve been checking out the new  @bubblemaps  V2 today, and there’s actually a lot more going on here than I expected.
The first thing that stood out to me is that V2 feels less like a tool you use just to look at a token, and more like a place where you can actually go through the whole process.
You can discover something, check the distribution, dig into the wallets, look at how things changed over time and even swap without jumping between different platforms.
That makes the whole experience feel much more natural.
One of the biggest changes is the new Trending and Fresh token feed, which is designed to filter out extremely high risk tokens and bundles before users buy. It covers tokens across chains, with Arc supported from day one.

The filters are also useful when you already have something specific in mind. You can narrow things down by chain, launchpad, price, volume, liquidity and more.
Once you find something interesting, you don't have to immediately open another website to start researching it.
You can simply hover over the token and get an instant bubble map preview.
That is probably one of the first things I would check before going any further.
The Bubblemaps Score adds another quick layer of information by highlighting things like bundled wallets and potential insider clusters.

From there, you can open the full map and actually look at how the holders are connected.
What I really liked is that the chart isn't separated from the onchain data either.
Click on a candle and you can see the holder distribution at that exact moment.

That gives you a different perspective because looking at the current holder distribution alone doesn't always tell the whole story. With Time Travel, you can go back and compare how the distribution changed over time.
And if you want to investigate deeper, Magic Nodes can help uncover connections through intermediary wallets that aren't always visible on the default map.
So instead of just asking “who holds this token?”, you can start asking better questions about how wallets are connected and how those relationships changed.
There are also some smaller details that make the whole experience feel more complete.
Project socials can be displayed on token pages after review, while wallet labels are reviewed by professional on chain sleuths before being published.
You can also customize what information you want to see while researching.
Then there is the built in swap.
If you have finished your research and decide you want to make a trade, you don't necessarily have to leave Bubblemaps to do it. The platform currently has a 0.5% fee for the built in swap, which Bubblemaps positions as the lowest fee on the market.
That is what I find interesting about the V2 direction.
It isn't trying to be just another token scanner or another charting dashboard.
The idea is more like:
Find → Vet → Analyze → Trade.
All from the same place.
There is also an in app boosting system for projects that want more visibility, while the broader Bubblemaps ecosystem is being built around $BMT 

The upcoming Intel Desk is especially interesting to me because it adds a community driven side to onchain research. Users can help prioritize investigations, vote on cases and contribute to the research process.
So after spending some time with V2, I can see why the revamp is more than just a visual update.
It brings discovery, holder analysis, historical data, wallet research and trading much closer together, while putting more focus on understanding risk before making a move.
If you haven't explored the revamped Bubblemaps platform yet, I think it is worth taking a look at the new V2 experience:

• Ether funds still hold over $1.5 billion in net inflows across the past 30 days
Third Straight Session of Ether ETF Outflows
U.S. spot spot Ethereum ETFs recorded roughly $39 million in net outflows on Thursday, a third consecutive session of withdrawals that stands in sharp contrast to the token's own price strength. Ether rose about 2% to near $2,470 over the same stretch, meaning institutional allocators kept trimming exposure even as the asset appreciated. The recent tape shows the pressure building: about $224 million left the funds on Wednesday and roughly $141 million on Tuesday, putting cumulative three-day outflows near $404 million. The monthly picture remains firmly positive, though — over the past 30 days, the Ethereum fund complex has still absorbed more than $1.5 billion in net creations, a cushion that keeps the institutional-adoption narrative intact despite the pullback.
The divergence is starker against bitcoin. Bitcoin ETFs pulled in roughly $159 million on Thursday while ether funds bled, and a single U.S. Zcash fund drew nearly $47 million — its strongest showing in a month that has brought it over $230 million — a sign that altcoin flows are rotating toward narrower, momentum-driven vehicles. Institutional demand for Ethereum-linked products is still expanding elsewhere: MoonPay is set to plug WisdomTree's tokenized treasury fund WTGXX into a network of some 35 million accounts. Macro conditions helped every major on Thursday: a day after the Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time since 2023, falling oil prices eased inflation fears, lifting the S&P 500 about 1% for its biggest advance in six weeks and the Nasdaq 100 nearly 2%. The 10-year Treasury yield snapped an eight-day rising streak as Brent crude settled under $105 a barrel. Crypto traded with, not ahead of, the equity tape.
Hoffman's Post-ETH Altcoin Rotation Pays Off
Bankless co-founder David Hoffman's decision to fully exit Ethereum on May 21 and redistribute into five altcoins has so far outperformed simply holding the asset, according to HTX pricing data. Hoffman disclosed entry prices for four of the five picks: NEAR Protocol near $1.40, Hyperliquid around $45, ZEC at roughly $560 and LIT at $1.35; his VVV entry was never made public. Measured at September 18 pricing, LIT had climbed about 272% to $5.02, ZEC roughly 170% to $1,512.42, NEAR about 149% to $3.49 and HYPE around 92% to $86.51 — every disclosed position beating ETH over the identical window. VVV, benchmarked to its May 21 print of $15.99 because the actual fill is undisclosed, was estimated up about 58% at $25.27.
Ethereum itself did not stand still. Over the same period HTX data shows ETH advancing from about $2,127.47 to $2,473.23, a roughly 16% gain — solid for a large cap, but clearly lagged by the higher-beta names Hoffman rotated into. The comparison carries caveats: percentage returns hinge on entry timestamps and benchmarks, and the VVV figure in particular rests on a time-stamped price rather than Hoffman's real cost basis. Still, the episode underscores a recurring pattern this cycle — capital rotating out of core ETH exposure into leveraged altcoin proxies built on its ecosystem, in search of outsized beta. Even after a regulatory stumble this month, when the Senate rejected the Clarity Act and ETH briefly slipped toward $2,388, the asset's foundation — the proof-of-stake settlement layer beneath a vast ecosystem of smart contract applications and Layer 2 scaling networks — remains the backdrop those trades are made against.

vos.title: Everyone Is Waiting for Altseason, but the Money Is Already Rotating‼️‼️‼️
vos.subTitle:
Everyone in crypto seems to be asking the same question.

When will altseason finally start?

Traders are watching Bitcoin dominance, ETH/BTC and every altcoin index they can find, waiting for one clear signal that says the entire altcoin market is ready to run.

But while everyone waits for the official confirmation, something interesting is already happening.

Money is moving.

Just not everywhere at once.

This Doesn't Look Like the Old Altseason Yet

A traditional altseason is easy to imagine.

Bitcoin rallies first. BTC eventually slows down. Ethereum begins outperforming. Large-cap altcoins follow, and eventually capital reaches smaller and more speculative tokens.

Suddenly almost everything seems to be green.

That broad move hasn't clearly arrived in 2026.

Bitcoin dominance was still around 59% in mid-September, showing that BTC continued to control a large share of the crypto market. Several altseason indicators also remained well below levels normally associated with a broad altcoin season.

So calling the current market a full altseason would be premature.

But that doesn't mean nothing is happening underneath Bitcoin.

The Rotation Is Becoming More Selective

Look deeper into the market and the picture changes.

Instead of money flowing into almost every altcoin, traders appear to be concentrating on specific sectors and individual tokens showing momentum.

Recent market-breadth data illustrates this clearly. On September 17, 89 of the 100 assets in KuCoin's QC100 index were advancing, while only 10 were declining. Meme-related assets and DeFi were among the strongest sectors in that snapshot, while Bitcoin's gain was much smaller.

Another market-breadth tracker showed strong recent performance across Layer 2, DeFi, meme, AI, RWA and Layer 1 categories, although methodologies differ between indexes and these short-term readings shouldn't be treated as proof of a lasting trend.

That's an important change.

The market may not be experiencing the classic "everything pumps" altseason.

Instead, it may be experiencing a rotation market.

Bitcoin Doesn't Need to Crash for Alts to Move

This is where many traders misunderstand rotation.

Money moving toward altcoins doesn't necessarily require Bitcoin to dump.

In fact, a sharp BTC decline can be bad for altcoins because fear spreads across the entire crypto market.

A more supportive environment can occur when Bitcoin becomes relatively stable.

If BTC holds its structure without absorbing all of the market's attention, traders may become more willing to look elsewhere for stronger percentage moves.

Bitcoin was around $76,000 on September 17 despite the Fed's latest rate increase and recent regulatory uncertainty.

That relative stability gives other parts of the market room to attract attention.

Follow Strength, Not the Word "Altseason"

This may be the biggest lesson from the current market.

Traders can become so focused on waiting for an official altseason that they miss the rotations happening directly in front of them.

One week, privacy coins may attract attention.

Another week, it could be DeFi.

Then Layer 1s, AI-related tokens, meme coins or another narrative could suddenly become the strongest part of the market.

That doesn't mean every narrative will continue rising.

It means capital is becoming selective.

Instead of asking only, "Has altseason started?", another useful question is:

"Where is the market showing relative strength right now?"

Bitcoin Dominance Still Matters

There is still one major obstacle to the classic altseason argument.

Bitcoin dominance remains elevated.

On September 13, one market tracker put BTC dominance at roughly 58.8%. Earlier September readings were around 59%.

For a much broader rotation, traders would generally want to see Bitcoin's share of the crypto market decline while altcoins consistently outperform BTC.

Ethereum is also important.

ETH/BTC strengthened substantially from its June lows and reached a seven-month high in August, an early indication that Ethereum had started gaining relative strength against Bitcoin. But Bitcoin dominance remained high at the same time, creating a mixed picture rather than a clean altseason signal.

That's why today's market needs more nuance than simply calling it Bitcoin season or altseason.

Not Every Altcoin Will Benefit

There is another major difference between today's market and older crypto cycles.

There are thousands of tokens competing for the same pool of attention and liquidity.

That makes it increasingly difficult for capital to lift the entire altcoin market equally.

Money can concentrate around a few strong narratives while hundreds of weaker tokens barely move.

This could make future rotations shorter and more aggressive.

A token can suddenly become the center of attention, move quickly, and then lose momentum as traders shift toward the next narrative.

That means simply owning an altcoin may not be enough to benefit from an altcoin rotation.

The market increasingly rewards attention, liquidity and relative strength.

The Real Signal Could Be Market Breadth

One giant altcoin candle isn't altseason.

Ten random coins pumping isn't necessarily altseason either.

What matters is whether strength begins spreading.

If more large-cap and mid-cap altcoins consistently outperform Bitcoin, market breadth continues improving and BTC dominance begins falling, the argument for a broader rotation becomes stronger.

Today's market is showing hints of that process, but the evidence remains mixed.

Bitcoin still controls a large portion of crypto's market value.

At the same time, capital is clearly finding opportunities below BTC.

Those two things can happen together.

The Bigger Picture

Maybe traders are waiting for altseason because they're expecting it to look exactly like previous cycles.

This cycle might be different.

Instead of one giant wave lifting almost every altcoin, we could see multiple smaller rotations moving through different narratives.

Privacy today.

DeFi tomorrow.

Layer 1s next.

Then perhaps another sector nobody is paying attention to yet.

The important thing isn't predicting which narrative comes next.

It's recognizing that the market doesn't have to declare "ALTSEASON" before capital starts moving.

Everyone is waiting for the rotation to begin.

The interesting part is that some of the money may already be rotating just not into everything at once.

I spent two years trading my way back from that hole, and if there is one thing I’ve learned, it’s that your profit doesn't exist until it is under your control. Think of an exchange like a public bus terminal. You can keep your luggage there while you’re waiting for the next ride, but you wouldn’t leave your life savings in a locker you don't hold the only key to. translatedData.title: Cardano YouTube channel hacked, broadcasting a scam impersonating Hoskinson
translatedData.subTitle:
Input Output warned users to avoid the project's YouTube channel $ADA  after it was suspected to have been hacked. The attackers broadcast a fake live stream impersonating Charles Hoskinson and claiming to distribute free coins.

As the company announced, the hacking incident was used to broadcast fraudulent content aimed at misleading viewers into believing there is a giveaway or free distribution related to the project. This is a common method that exploits the names of prominent figures in the industry to lure victims.
